issues.description: STTv2 class name complects API versioning with the type itself
issues.detail: The 'v2' lives in the class name rather than as data (a model_id or capability). Now every caller's import statement is coupled to ElevenLabs' product versioning. Deepgram repeated this mistake; that is not justification. A single STT class parameterized by model is simpler — one concept, the model is just a value passed in.

issues.description: Commit strategy hardcoded despite type Literal advertising choice
issues.detail: STTCommitStrategy is exported as a type with multiple values, but _connect_ws hardcodes 'commit_strategy=vad'. The type lies about the data. Either the strategy is a value the caller passes (simple — one piece of data flowing through) or it is not configurable and the Literal should be removed. Pick one; do not advertise a knob that does not exist.

issues.description: _speaking boolean complects identity, value, and time across event types
issues.detail: A mutable boolean tracks 'are we in a speech segment' while three branches (partial_transcript, committed_transcript with text, committed_transcript empty) each read and mutate it. Speech-segment identity is intertwined with transcript value and event ordering. Model the segment as an explicit value with a clear lifecycle, or derive it from message_type — do not place-orient it across handlers.

issues.description: audio_format derived from sample_rate yet both stored as separate fields
issues.detail: audio_format is computed as f'pcm_{sample_rate}' and stored alongside sample_rate in STTOptions. Two fields, one fact. If sample_rate changes, audio_format silently drifts. Either store sample_rate alone and derive the format string at the WebSocket boundary, or accept the format as the input. One source of truth per fact.

issues.description: Query string assembled by hand instead of as data
issues.detail: params is built as a list of pre-formatted f-strings, then joined. The structure (a mapping of name to optional value) is flattened too early into strings, losing the ability to inspect, log, or test the parameters as values. A dict filtered for non-None and passed to aiohttp's params= is simpler and avoids manual escaping concerns later.

issues.description: Example file uses VAD parameters with no relationship to STT VAD knobs
issues.detail: realtime_scribe_v2.py passes vad_silence_threshold_secs and vad_threshold to STTv2 while also wiring silero.VAD into the session. Two independent VADs with similarly named knobs. A user reading this cannot tell which VAD owns which threshold. Either name the STT-side knobs to mark them as server-side (e.g. server_vad_*) or document the two-VAD model explicitly.

review.summary: The integration works but it is easy, not simple. The 'v2' suffix complects API versioning with the Python type — the same concept (an STT that talks to ElevenLabs) is now split across two classes because the vendor incremented a number; that complexity is incidental and will compound on v3. Inside the stream, a mutable _speaking flag braids segment identity, transcript value, and event ordering across three branches, which is exactly the place-oriented pattern that produces subtle bugs under reconnect or out-of-order messages. The commit_strategy Literal advertises a knob the code hardcodes, audio_format duplicates sample_rate, and the example layers two VADs with overlapping names. The question that should have been asked first: what is the smallest set of values flowing through this stream — model, audio config, segment state — and can one STT class take them as data instead of two classes growing in parallel?
